summary: This is a sound stage-2 rewrite. It takes the stage-1 kernel, which was correct but structurally serial, and gives it FA3's own structure (warp-specialized producer, 128-key tiles, intra-WG overlap, ping-pong), with a hard per-class gate so every outcome is flat or better. Proceed, after fixing four things in the brief: the base is stale (the contiguous-KV FA3 path is now master's first_turn incumbent), the exp-offload clamp contradicts Max_offset 8, the earlier exp-offload run goes uncited, and the M2 target is optimistic.
justification:
A. The mechanism is plausible. At head_dim 64 there are 256 MMA FLOP per exponential. MUFU ex2 runs 16/clk/SM, so the exp floor (for ft ctx65536: 16384 x ~73.7K avg keys x 16 heads = 1.93e10 exps at 3.87e12/s, about 5.0 ms) sits about 2x above the FP8 tensor floor (~2.5 ms). The quoted 555/2770/4990/1000/250 us floors check out. FA3 at ~1.6x that floor means its exp and MMA overlap is imperfect, and a stage-1 kernel with wait_group 0 after every wgmma, 64-key tiles and no warp specialization could not overlap at all. That explains its 1.53-1.67x (log 306cbde58aff4fa4: GATE 675/2725/1383/6990/12602 us vs FA3 425/1633/906/4496/8076). Per-thread resources fit: two 64x128 fp32 S buffers take 128 regs, O takes 32, P fragments about 16, all under setmaxnreg 232. Smem is 3 x 24 KB + 8 KB Q, about 80 KB at 1 CTA/SM. The producer moves 16 KB of gather plus 8 KB of transpose per ~1024-clk tile, which is easy.

WEAKEST LINK: the M2 target of 0.8x FA3 (~1.34x the exp floor). The structure this stage adds is FA3's own structure, so it should be expected to reach about FA3 (M1), not beat it. The only real differentiator is the FMA-pipe exp offload, and it pays only if MUFU is the binding unit. The issue budget is roughly FFMA + FMNMX + FADD + 0.5 F2FP + permute, about 4.5 slots per element at 128/clk/SM, about 0.035 clk/elem against MUFU's 0.0625. Offloading 2/8 adds about 1.75 slots: issue rises to about 0.049 and MUFU falls to about 0.047, a ~22% ceiling. At 3/8, issue (~0.055) binds. So 0.7-0.8x needs better-than-FA3 latency hiding AND MUFU saturation at the same time. Read M1 as success for this stage.

STALE BASE AND NUMBERS. The brief says 'port onto 1932a9c4; attention code unchanged'. Master is now 61ce79bb. fa3-full-contiguous-kv-triton-gather-gated (020566aa) landed and routes contig-varlen FA3 (path B) at all three first_turn classes: 7627/4247/862 us vs paged 8025/4466/901 in the 73b40cd13fdf4bb0 log, and 7736.5/4304.5 us in the best profile. Paged FA3 (A) stays at turn_1/turn_4. The expected-block FA3 numbers (8352.6/4542.4/911.7) are about 5-8% high at first_turn, so the M2 bars should be about 6190/3440/690 us against the real incumbent.

PRIOR. The frontmatter has no `prior` field. depends_on names stage 1 (the real predecessor), but the body never cites attn-full-prefill-cuda-fp8-exp-offload (regression 0.8813x, job f5c30b15fd284c15). That run's wgmma build failed, and an mma.sync fallback WITH 2/8 FMA exp offload went live and lost on every full shape. This is a different engine (wgmma, warp-specialized), so it is not a duplicate. It is still the only judge evidence on exp offload and it was negative. The EXP_SW=0 instance in the gate is the right answer to it, and should be described that way. Nothing on DIAGNOSIS's do-not-try list matches. DIAGNOSIS lists this as action 5: valid, with a lower ceiling than the rega multicast actions.

EXPECTED. The directions are consistent with TASK weights. Full-layer FA3 is 12.8/16.4/9.1% of the three loads, so a gated run is flat at worst and about +2-3% headline at M2. Sliding flat is correct.
confounders: fa3-full-contiguous-kv-triton-gather-gated (landed 020566aa): it owns full-layer attention routing at first_turn (mode B contig-varlen, ~0.95x paged incl. gather). If the s2 gate times paged FA3 as the brief literally says ('FA3 with its combine', '<= 0.95 x FA3, else FA3 exactly as master'), its bar is wrong at all three first_turn classes. An s2 at 0.93x paged is only ~0.98x the real incumbent and would be routed on a margin inside noise. In kernel_fn, the s2 branch must also sit ahead of the fa3c route lookup and fall back to master's routed (A or B) call, not to bare paged FA3. The gate's incumbent must be state['fa3c']['route'][key] per class, so _attn_s2 setup has to run after _fa3c_setup.

combo-a-master-normgather-naive-stack / combo-b (landed): expert-side only, no stream overlap with attention (the router side stream starts after attention), so no kernel-level confound. They do add to prepare time (~140 s now) and memory. The three-instance load_inline build happens at import and counts against the 15-minute run limit.
No other landed hypothesis touches the full-layer attention launch, its bytes or its numerics.
interference: No companion is needed. This is a rewrite stage behind a hard per-class gate, and the run is read from its own GATE lines (FA3-incumbent vs sw0 vs sw2 vs sw3, per class) and the profile's top_kernels, not from the headline. The one sub-change worth isolating, exp offload, is already isolated in the same run: EXP_SW=0 is compiled and timed beside 2 and 3. A revert of fa3-contiguous is not needed either. The fix is to make the gate compare against master's actually routed incumbent per class (contig B at first_turn, paged A at turns) and to log both numbers. Per today's lesson on 1.02x prepare selectors, the 0.95 bar is already well clear of noise. The gate should still run two interleaved rounds (alternating incumbent and candidates, >= 25 replays each) and route only if both rounds clear 0.95 with the IQR bound printed. The candidate pick among sw0/2/3 should require a >= 3% separation, else take sw0 (the simplest).
rules_flags: Exp-offload clamp vs Max_offset: the brief clamps x to [-127, 0] AND packs P with FA3's Max_offset 8 (P in [0, 256]). If the offset is folded into the FFMA as FA3 does (x = s*scale - (max*scale - 8), x up to +8), the clamp caps offloaded columns at P = 1 while MUFU columns reach 256: a 256x per-column error. This is a correctness bug, not a rule breach, but it would exclude or fail every offload instance. Fix: clamp the un-offset argument to [-127, 0], evaluate the polynomial, then add (j + 8) << 23, or clamp to [-119, 8] consistently on both paths.

Host syncs / branching on values: the persistent longest-first item list and split counts must be built from shapes only (batch, q_len, page_table width; the class key as stage 1 and fa3c use). Per-request ragged lengths come from cache_seqlens read on device. No host read of cache_seqlens or cu_seqlens_q in kernel_fn.

Precision: P rounded to E4M3 with Max_offset matches FA3's own FP8 path, and a ~1e-4 polynomial 2^x is far below E4M3 rounding, so it is fine. Q stays at E4M3, no coarser. No issue as specified. If a later stage switches to ex2.approx.f16x2 (the DIAGNOSIS suggestion), get the rules check first, as DIAGNOSIS says.
Every key: masked columns going to ~0 via the clamp is causal masking, not skipping. No block-skipping or attention-weight-based value skipping is described. OK.

Fault safety: setmaxnreg with a mismatched launch shape or a bad mbarrier phase faults and poisons the context (LESSONS). The brief already requires __launch_bounds__(384,1), -lineinfo, per-launch sync+print canaries, and okc check only. Keep those.
open_questions: Gate incumbent: will the builder rebase onto 61ce79bb and time master's routed path (contig-varlen B incl. its gather at first_turn, paged A at turns) as the incumbent, with the s2 branch placed before the fa3c lookup in kernel_fn? The expected-block FA3 numbers should be updated to 7736.5/4304.5/~860/1648.7/424.1 us.
Is the exp-offload argument range consistent with Max_offset 8 (see rules_flags)? The exp2 unit test should cover x in [-127, 8] and compare offloaded vs MUFU columns on the same row.

F2FP (fp32 -> e4m3x2 pack) and the accumulator-to-A-fragment permute also compete for issue slots. Would per-instance cycle counters (clock64 around softmax vs wgmma waits, as the ssdq counters did) let stage 3 see which unit binds?

Could s2 at first_turn read the contiguous K/V that fa3c's gather already produces (8-17 us) and load it by TMA instead of a cp.async row gather? That would simplify the producer and remove the per-row page-table indirection where the gather is cheap.

Build time: three template instances of a heavier warp-specialized kernel at import (stage 1 took 31 s for one). Log the compile time, and drop EXP_SW=3 if the build exceeds ~90 s, so the 15-minute run limit is not at risk on top of ~140 s of prepare.

L2->SM ingest: a 128-query-row item re-reads K/V once per 128 rows (FA3's hdim64 tile is larger in M). At the M2 rate this needs roughly 3-4 TB/s L2->SM, a meaningful fraction of the ~6 TB/s ceiling the rega logs measured. Is a 192-row item (3 consumer WGs) worth considering in stage 3 if s2 lands near FA3?
